citation.title: Roentgen-cephalometric standards for a Swedish population. A longitudinal study between the ages of 5 and 31 years

curation.notes: Compared 2026-10-08 (norms:compare a vs b exit 1, 394 differences: set n by sex 2 (a left them out); source wording 238; definitionMatch 84 (NL/NSL, ML/NSL, n–ss–pg, UIL/NL, UIL/n–ss mm, LIL/n–sm mm, 14 rows each); 70 rows only b entered (n–gn, s–tgo, sp′–gn, sp′–gn/n–gn, SPg–npgL × 2 sexes × 7 ages). Every mean, SD and n of the 238 rows both entered agreed. Checked against the page images: all of Table 6 (p. 376; b read it from the text layer, merge notes) and all 70 b-only rows on Tables 5-8 (pp. 375-378) - agree; the convexity conversions (e.g. men 170.2 → 9.8 ... 181.2 → −1.2) re-done from the image. Decisions: (1) definitionMatch: NL/NSL #26 and UIL/NL #55 a same, b close → close (nasal line through pm, not PNS; merge notes); ML/NSL #90 a same, b close → close (tangent ML vs constructed gonion-menton; merge notes); n–ss–pg #5 a close, b same → same (same points; 180 − full angle is the catalogue's departure from straight, + convex; the conversion is noted on each row); incisor mm #46/#49 a same, b close → close (point and sign not stated; merge notes). (2) b-only rows kept after the page check: n–gn → #41 close (gn not Me); s–tgo → #40 close (constructed gonion); sp′–gn → #28 close and sp′–gn/n–gn → #29 close (sp′ and gn for ANS and Me); SPg–npgL → #83 different, kept but never used (soft-tissue pogonion level, perpendicular to N–Pog; the catalogue measures at suprapogonion level between the two facial lines). (3) Source: one wording, table, page, paper row and age group. (4) Age bands: Table 4's observed range of each age group (both extractors), written in completed years ([4,5], [6,8], [9,11], [12,13], [14,17], [18,20], [29,32]) because the resolver places a patient by completed years (P12): a band of 6.6–8.2 would leave out a child of 6 y 9 m, who is '6' in completed years though inside the group's observed range. The nominal ages (5, 7, ...) were not used: as single-age bands they would leave most ages uncovered. Bands of one measurement and sex do not overlap. (5) Selection a class-I, b class-I-balanced → class-I-balanced: the inclusion criteria include a 'straight' profile without obvious asymmetry (p. 371). (6) Scale enlarged 10%, p. 372 (the 10 per cent enlargement was not corrected in the linear distances; each table's caption repeats the 10 per cent magnification). n per row: Table 3's radiographs for that sex and age group. Ruling P50 (8 Oct): SPg–npgL #83 different -> close (same quantity at another level/direction). Caveat added: identical male and female SDs of sp′–gn/n–gn in all seven age groups.

caveats: Sample: 'normal' Swedes from two groups, Umeå (group U, 7-31 y, mixed-longitudinal then longitudinal) and Enköping (group E, 5-13 y, longitudinal): Angle Class I molar/canine relationship, normal transverse occlusion, overjet and overbite 1-3 mm, no congenitally missing teeth or crowding, a 'straight' profile without obvious asymmetry, no orthodontic treatment (pp. 371-372). Groups U and E did not differ at 7, 10 and 13 y and were combined (p. 372).

The counts are radiographs, not people: the same children were filmed at several ages (Table 3, p. 372; Figure 2), so the 469 films (205 male, 264 female) come from far fewer individuals, and the age groups are not independent samples.

Linear (mm) values include the films' 10% enlargement (p. 372: the 10 per cent enlargement was not corrected in the linear distances); the app shows them at true size (÷ 1.10) with the printed value. Angles and % are unaffected.
Age bands are each group's observed age range (Table 4, p. 373, both sexes together), written in completed years: 4-5, 6-8, 9-11, 12-13, 14-17, 18-20 and 29-32 y. Ages 21-28 have no group.

Landmarks follow Björk (1947): sp′ (nasal line ∩ n–pg line) and tgo (mandibular line ∩ ramus line) are constructed points, the nasal line runs through pm (pterygomaxillare) and the mandibular line is the lower-border tangent through gn (pp. 373-374, Fig 3). Rows using them are close.
Convexity n–ss–pg is printed as the full angle (168.7-181.4°); stored as 180 minus the printed mean (the departure from straight, + convex), SD unchanged.

Soft-tissue chin SPg–npgL (Tables 7-8) is entered as #83, close (ruling P50): the same quantity, soft-tissue chin thickness, but measured at soft-tissue pogonion, perpendicular to N–Pog, while the catalogue's #83 is at suprapogonion level between the bony and soft-tissue facial lines.
Head position: cephalostat, maximal intercuspal position (p. 372); no reference plane for orientation is stated, and FH is not used in any measurement.

Not in the catalogue: n–s–ba; s–n; s–ar; sp′–pm (maxillary length); n–sp′ and n–sp′/n–gn (%); s–n–pg; ar–tgo; tgo–gn; ar–pg; n–gn/s–tgo (%) (the reciprocal of the Jarabak ratio: not converted, as the SD of a reciprocal cannot be derived from the printed SD); soft-tissue P–, Sn–, SLS–, Ls–, St–, Li– and ILS–npgL (Tables 5-8). Body height (Figure 5) is not a cephalometric measurement.
sp′–gn/n–gn (%) (#29): identical male and female SDs in all seven age groups, as printed in both tables — possibly a misprint.
